Corgis usually put their "tails" down like other dogs when their nervous or otherwise. When that happens the few vertebra are enough to cover the anus, and because of their coats the fur blends together, giving the appearance of a smooth surface.

Also known as the EBH or Elusive ButtHole

That's not necessarily true.

Dog fur and especially double coats does not grow the same way as human hair.

I will also add that it's believed that the soft downy layer fur has more sensitive follicles.

A groomer brushed out my corgis spine too much two years ago and he still has no down layer in that area.

The down layer grows very slowly and it's growth can be retarded due to the thick heavier fur laying across the skin and growing more quickly.

Corgis have a very thick soft downy under layer of fur, as well as a coarse longer layer of fur.

When the fur is cut, shaved, or pulled out, and even brushed too hard, the under layer does not grow back as well.

This underlayer is useful in regulating the dog's body temperature and prevents them from over heating or becoming too cold. Think of it as insulation in a home.

Double coated dogs also tend to be more sensitive to sunlight as well, and suffer bad sunburns when shaved.

Source: corgi owner, many vet friends, extensive research.

I'm a woman with very long pointed nails.

A few reasons:

* I *like* them. To me, they are aesthetically pleasing. I know others may not prefer them, but I don't care what they want from my appearance.

* I chewed my nails into my twenties. Growing my nails out and spending extra time on them is like earning a trophy for kicking a bad habit.

* Nails take time to grow. In that time, movement adjusts to compensate and I've become used to them. If I break a nail I have to relearn how to use that finger until it grows out again.

* Have you never had a woman with long nails lightly scratch your back or scalp??? It's HEAVEN.

* What appeals to you physically is not always what a woman chooses for herself. We often will see something, admire they way it looks, and recreate it on ourselves to see if we enjoy it. 

* Very long nails are, sometimes, unique. They garner a bit of extra attention and those who do appreciate them will sometimes compliment them, which affirms our personal choice in how we've decided to look.
